concerns.text: The chi-squared test (FR-015) requires annotated logs in BOTH high-drift and low-drift bins, but the only annotated set defined is the FR-017 'random sample of >=100 logs across the full drift range'. If the high/low bins are extreme quantiles (e.g. top/bottom 10%), a uniform full-range sample of 100 logs yields only ~10-20 logs per bin, leaving the chi-squared test badly underpowered and prone to empty-cell failures. The plan must specify how bin membership is ensured in the annotation sample (e.g. stratified oversampling of both bins in addition to the full-range sample) and the expected per-bin annotated counts.

Construct validity: GitHub issue threads are bug reports / user discussions, not 'agent interaction logs'. The drift detector is built on agent-conversation centroids from agentdog/safety-v1, but the novel corpus is a different text genre. If drift scores and human 'novel attack' labels are driven by genre/format differences rather than safety-content differences, the validation confounds source with construct. The plan needs either a documented mapping step (how an issue thread becomes an agent-interaction log) or an explicit acknowledgment + analysis of this confound (e.g. reporting results split by source).

Latency comparison protocol is underspecified for the drift method: per-log latency for the drift pipeline depends on whether the embedding is computed batched (batch 64) or singly. State explicitly that drift per-log latency is measured with batch size 1 (or amortized batched throughput) and that both methods use identical input text and warm-up, so the <= 0.5x claim is well-defined.
